TThe House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to make adequate budgetary provisions in the 2027 Appropriation Bill for the completion of abandoned and uncompleted projects in Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency of Ondo State. The House also urged the Federal Government to dispatch a fact-finding delegation to Aiyetoro community to assess the extent of sea incursion threatening the coastal settlement and audit projects allegedly abandoned across the constituency. The resolutions followed the unanimous adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved at plenary on Wednesday by the member representing Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency, Mr Donald Ojogo. Moving the motion, Ojogo said the constituency remained the only oil-producing federal constituency in the South-West, contributing more than 60,000 barrels of crude oil daily to the nation’s production output. He, however, lamented that despite its contribution to the national economy, the area had continued to suffer neglect, with several critical infrastructure projects either abandoned after commencement or left without adequate funding. The lawmaker warned that the continued neglect of the projects had generated growing discontent among residents, particularly youths, with concerns that the situation could degenerate into protests and a possible disruption of oil production in the area. He said the growing agitation over the plight of the communities required urgent intervention and assurances from the Federal Government to prevent a breakdown of law and order. The planned threat of shutdown of oil production in the area over the plight of the people, especially as it relates to Aiyetoro should be particularly disturbing,” he said. Ojogo’s motion also drew attention to the environmental challenges confronting Aiyetoro, a coastal community in the Ilaje area that has faced persistent sea incursion and shoreline erosion, threatening homes, livelihoods and other critical infrastructure. The community’s vulnerability to coastal erosion has remained a longstanding concern, with residents repeatedly calling for effective shoreline protection measures to prevent further destruction and displacement. Following the adoption of the motion, the House urged the federal government to send “a fact-finding delegation to Aiyetoro community to confirm the extent of the tamable but overlooked sea incursion that has ravaged the oil-rich areas of Ilaje and as well take an audit of the highlighted abandoned projects.” The lawmakers also urged the House Committee on Appropriation to ensure that adequate funds were provided in the 2027 budget for the completion of the identified projects and other interventions capable of improving the living conditions of residents.
